summary: 110-foot steel tower in Garrett County, Maryland, built late 1930s on state land; NHLR-registered 2018; carried state communications gear by 2007, with no legal access to the site.

access.note: Tower site is state-owned, but the access road is privately owned and legal access to the site is not possible. The tower can be seen from Maryland Route 42.

events.note: State of Maryland acquired the site in January 1934
As of 2007 the tower hosted communications equipment for the Maryland Forest Service and Garrett County EMS

notes_for_editor: Built year: the register says only 'late 1930s' with no exact year, so no built event is recorded (an earlier 1938 placeholder was removed as unsupported). No staffing history, notable fires or visit information was found in the sources read, so those keys are omitted. Web posts (a Reddit thread and abandonedonline.net) say the tower dates to about 1934 and was decommissioned with the land returned to a private owner. These were not fetched or cited and conflict with the 2006 DNR report and 2007 NHLR status; the story leaves them out. The DNR synopsis table (Elder Hill row: 110 ft, condition Good, communications equipment present, reversion clause yes) agrees with the story but is not cited. The DNR report is a draft and the story says so.
